journey.name: Signup — the phone number's country is picked, not typed
journey.description:
SMS verification is limited per number, weekly and yearly, and both limits are terminal — so a number sent in the wrong shape costs an attempt the user does not get back. The country picker exists so nobody has to know their calling code or remember to drop a trunk 0.
Stops before "Send code": sending spends a real SMS attempt.

actions.action: From a signed-out Loopky, tap "onboarding_create_pubky", then "signup_method_sms"
Verify "signup_phone_country" shows the device region's flag and calling code (an en-US emulator shows 🇺🇸 +1), and "signup_phone_hint" reads "Choose your country, then enter your number."
Tap "signup_phone_country". Verify a full-height sheet titled "Country" lists every country by name in the app's language, each with its calling code
Type "bra" into the search field. Verify Brazil is listed and the sheet keeps its height while the list shrinks
Clear it and type "+49". Verify only Germany remains — the search matches calling codes too
Search "brazil" and tap it. Verify the sheet closes and the button reads 🇧🇷 +55
Type 86998006407 into "signup_phone_input". Verify the hint turns into "We'll text +55 86998006407." and "Send code" is enabled
Replace the number with +447700900123 (as a paste or autofill would give it). Verify the button moves to 🇬🇧 +44 and the field keeps only 7700900123 — the calling code is never doubled
Replace the number with 07700900123. Verify the hint still reads "We'll text +44 7700900123." — the trunk 0 is dropped
